items.title: OpenAI's Four-Part Prompt Recipe
points: The four components: result you want, who it's for, context and limits, and what done looks like—each fills a gap where AI otherwise makes assumptions.
Leaving details unstated forces the model to guess on decisions that matter: tone, length, audience context, and success criteria.
OpenAI research shows adding more words to prompts actually degrades results; the four-part structure outperforms longer instructions because models now read nuance efficiently.
Example: 'Write a toast for my sister's wedding' is vague; specifying length, humor level, attendees, and format prevents AI from inventing details you wouldn't choose.

items.title: Hacker News Scores AI's Ten-Year Goals
points: 9,694 voters cast 100,590 votes on AI challenges from 2016-2024; writing working code from plain sentences reached 87% achievement, while self-driving in all conditions stayed at 78% not achieved.

Pattern shows screen-based tasks fall first: AI learned code by reading code examples, but physical tasks require understanding pressure, grip, and environmental variation with no clear training data.
Robot toilet-cleaning remains 69% unachieved; the challenge isn't the concept but the lack of video data showing how hard to press or brush angle—unlike code, where examples are abundant.
Sample bias: voters self-selected from Hacker News audience, not a random population, so results reflect that community's assessment.

items.title: Neuralink's Brain Implant Reaches Multi-Week Stability
points: Problem: brain signals shift over time as implant threads move and neurons change, forcing users to recalibrate decoders (software that translates brain signals into actions) daily (~10 minutes) to maintain cursor accuracy.
Solution: AI trained on 50,000+ hours of accumulated patient brain data over two years enables the decoder to recognize signal shifts and adapt without manual recalibration.
Result: decoders now stay accurate for weeks instead of days; some participants reduced calibration from daily to ~10 minutes weekly.
Significance: daily resets would make brain implants unusable; weekly or longer intervals transform them from experimental devices into reliable tools people depend on.

items.title: Audible Interactive Stories and AI Character Guides
points: Audiobook feature shows character identity on player as story plays, plus spoiler-free cards for each character—solving confusion when full casts narrate multiple roles.
Interactive Stories let listeners respond to book characters in real time; first release features Renfield from Dracula's Servant; new interactive titles roll out monthly.
Change: audiobooks traditionally talk at listeners; this breaks that one-way model, pausing narrative to wait for user input and respond—creating bidirectional conversation within fiction.
Adoption risk: feature only available on select titles now; wider uptake depends on listener interest and author participation.

items.title: Meta Home Link Smart Home Router
points: Meta releases Home Link, a USB-C router device running AI assistant Muse to control smart home devices like TVs and lights without remotes.
